newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK global trade, non-EU trade.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK global trade, non-EU trade.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK global trade data for January and non-EU trade data for February.
The data showed the global trade gap was 641 million stg in Jan, the Feb non-EU trade gap 554 million stg.

"The global figures are a little better than expected. That's a result of high export demand. This is evidence the UK's trade performance is yet to suffer from the pound's appreciation and certainly suggests the trade performance is nothing to worry about."
"There is some danger for the year ahead that the loss of competitiveness the pound's rise has incurred could cause the trade deficit to widen."

"They are a bit better than expected. The markets will be interested in the export side and looking at the global figures exports are showing decent gains in nominal terms anyway. So some of the worries over the rise of the pound and the loss of competitiveness may be overdone. In terms of the pound it's a small plus."

"The figures are bang in line with expectations. But these numbers aren't really telling us a trememdous amount at the moment. It's later in the year that we're going to see the full effect of sterling and strong domestic demand on these numbers. At the moment you've got the lagged effect of sterling being quite weak in the middle of last year and also the price effects are helping the trade balance at the moment. We're not seeing any great trend in these numbers but we would expect them to deteriorate in the second half of the year."
